observations: Photo 0: Camera body clearly marked 'Nikon' on front plate and 'Z fc' engraved near top right; rear lens cap reads 'Nikon Z mount'.
Photo 1: Top dial shows ISO markings (100–51200) and shutter speed dial; 'Z fc' text visible on body; attached lens is a manual-focus lens with aperture ring marked in both feet and meters.
Photo 2: Top-down view shows camera with battery, Nikon-branded charger, two rear lens caps, and a front lens cap marked 'TTArtisan APS-C 25mm f2.0'.
No screen-on, shutter-count, or power-up shot is visible in any photo.
No visible damage, but sensor, mount condition, and internal function cannot be judged from stills.

claims.claim: Nikon Z fc, retro-inspired SLR-style mirrorless camera, 20.9MP APS-C sensor
claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show 'Nikon' and 'Z fc' markings matching this description.
Photo 0 clearly shows 'Nikon' branding and 'Z mount' lens cap, not Canon.
Photo 2 shows a Nikon-branded battery and charger alongside the camera.

claims.claim: Lens included is a Nikon lens
claims.evidence: Photo 2 cap reads 'TTArtisan APS-C 25mm f2.0', a third-party manual lens, not a Nikon-branded lens.

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or sensor may be faulty
risks.proof: A video or photo of the camera powered on showing the rear screen and a live image

risks.risk: Shutter count unknown, could be heavily used
risks.proof: A screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or EXIF data

risks.risk: Lens compatibility and condition (third-party manual lens, not Nikon OEM)
risks.proof: Close-up photo of lens glass and mount, plus confirmation of autofocus/manual operation
risks.if_unproven: priced as bundled third-party lens, not Nikon kit lens value

risks.risk: Mismatch between listed brand text ('Canon') and actual item (Nikon) suggests careless or copy-pasted listing
risks.proof: Seller confirmation or corrected listing text matching photographed brand
risks.if_unproven: treated as a listing error, not affecting the physical item's identity, but lowers seller reliability

proof_requests: Video of camera powering on, showing screen and shutter firing
Photo of shutter count or menu firmware screen
Close-up of lens mount and glass for scratches or fungus
Photo of memory card slot and battery contacts for corrosion
response.reason: Photos clearly identify the item as a Nikon Z fc body with a third-party TTArtisan lens despite the seller text's false 'Canon' claim; functionality is unverified so it is priced at worst case pending a power-on proof.
